task: T5: add the two static checks on the gate itself to scripts/gate-selftest.sh. First, coverage: collect every assertion id the task's `verify.sh` uses in its own `ok` and `no` calls, collect every id declared by a mutant, and fail the run naming any gate id that no mutant declares. An assertion no mutant exercises has never been observed to work, which is the same state as one that cannot fail — mutation testing detects a weak assertion, but only this check detects an unexercised one. Second, the `pend` ban: fail the run naming the file if the task's `verify.sh` INVOKES `pend` — a line where it appears as a command, such as at the start of a line or after `then`, `else`, `do`, `;`, `&&` or `||`. Ban the verb, not the word: a gate that merely mentions `pend` in a comment or in an assertion message must pass, and gates in this very spec do exactly that because they are the ones asserting the ban. A check that cannot tell a call from a mention would fail its own author's correct work, which is how `specs/lib/assert.sh` was nearly given an impossible instruction. A per-task gate asserts only its own task's criteria, so it has nothing to defer, and `specs/lib/assert.sh` deliberately does not define the verb. Fold both failures into the exit code the run already returns from T4. Add no new mutant handling and change no verdict logic.
